question.problem:
What is ${\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a right Riemann sum?

*Hint: Write down the missing expression in terms of $i$ and $n.$*

${\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}$
{{field-1}}
$\cdot \,\frac{\pi }{6n}$
question.worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a right Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx,
$$

where ${x}_{i}=a+iΔx$ and $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x),$ the lower bound is $a=0$ and the upper bound is $b=\pi /6.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{\pi /6-0}{n}=\frac{\pi }{6n}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}f(0+i\cdot \frac{\pi }{6n})\cdot \frac{\pi }{6n} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}f(\frac{\pi i}{6n})\cdot \frac{\pi }{6n} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\cdot \frac{\pi i}{6n})\cdot \frac{\pi }{6n} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi i}{2n})\cdot \frac{\pi }{6n}.\end{aligned}
$$
